description.p: YarmiplayServerTV runs a Syncplay server and a Jellyfin server from the system tray, so friends can watch videos in sync from your media library with YarmiplayTV or any Syncplay client.

ul.li: A Syncplay 1.7.6 compatible server with rooms, an optional password, chat and a shared playlist
A Jellyfin media server, set up from the control panel
Works with a Plex Media Server you install yourself: manage its libraries and share it with your Syncplay users
Optional UPnP port forwarding so people outside your home network can connect
Free encrypted connections with a DuckDNS domain and a Let's Encrypt certificate
Starts with your session and keeps running in the tray

description.p: Jellyfin is developed by the Jellyfin project and included unmodified under its own license. Plex is a trademark of Plex, Inc.; Plex Media Server is not included and this app is not made or endorsed by Plex.

description.p: The tray icon uses the same crop as the app icon, so it fills the tray slot.
Voice chat in Syncplay rooms, relayed through this PC and not recorded. The Windows setup upgrades an older MSI install and keeps settings.
Refresh libraries removes a Jellyfin library when its folders are missing or empty, without deleting any files.
Refresh libraries on the Jellyfin page scans every library and reloads the list.
The desktop icon fills its tile.
Password or approved devices can add a YarmiplayTV device to the approved list when it joins with the password. On by default.
New app icon: a server rack with the YarmiplayTV play prism.
App icon: the server and orbit fill the tile, with less empty margin around them.
New app icon: the server in the center, with the YarmiplayTV play prism on its orbit.
Brand identity update: prominent central server blade chassis with orbiting crystalline play prism satellite
New 3D brand identity with server blade chassis and streamlined orbital sync
Jellyfin: connection-driven instant self-healing with proxy decoupling and resilient SQLite retries; auto-update check frequency updated to every 30 minutes.
Jellyfin: server owns Jellyfin with automatic database administrator session recovery; website: dedicated Setup and Internet Access guide pages.
Jellyfin's HTTPS port sends the full certificate chain, like the Syncplay port, so older devices connect without extra roots; renewed certificates no longer restart Jellyfin
HTTPS with a domain of your own, not only DuckDNS: the certificate is validated on port 80, which UPnP forwards with the servers
The server's home addresses only go to the people it lets in, and leave out virtual machine, WSL and VPN adapters.
Jellyfin: sort loose episodes into show folders, once or as they arrive
Port forwarding (UPnP) can be switched on from the Dashboard
Browsers can join rooms at tv.yarmiplay.com/watch
Room settings shared by everyone in a room, starting with skipping anime openings and endings in YarmiplayTV.
Encrypted connections from home: YarmiplayTV finds the server on the local network and verifies the DuckDNS certificate, and the DuckDNS name now also gets this PC's IPv6 address.
Managed Syncplay rooms: only room operators can play, pause and seek, and the host can create managed rooms from the Syncplay page.
Works with your own Plex Media Server: manage its libraries from the control panel and share it with your Syncplay users through Plex friend invites. Plex is not included; install it from plex.tv.

The Syncplay server can now require the password from everyone, including approved devices, the message of the day is now a welcome message clients show when they join, and the server reports itself as Syncplay 1.7.6.
The Jellyfin page no longer warns about a missing Syncplay password when only approved devices can join, and renaming an approved device is tidier.

Viewers in a room can now stream or download a video another YarmiplayTV viewer has through a cached file relay, the host can share Jellyfin with Syncplay users through a guest account and the Syncplay port, and a vanilla Syncplay mode turns all of it off.
The host can also let in only the YarmiplayTV devices they approve, so no password needs to be shared.
Available on the Snap Store for Linux, with Jellyfin built in; the Snap Store keeps it up to date.
Tidier Syncplay settings: the fields line up in two columns and the password's Show button sits inside its box.
Updates get their own card on the dashboard, and a new About screen links to the website, YarmiplayTV and the source code.
Packaging improvements for the Microsoft Store.
Automatic updates from GitHub releases, and the control panel can be opened in a web browser on the same computer.
First release.
